meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did Owen find out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He drafts somewhere else and pastes it in. That's a word processor, not a confession.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote from memory. Is one wrong line your whole case?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Then whatever happens next, it stays off his record and it stays quiet, and you still haven't answered me about his record.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. I'll agree to that to put this behind him, not because he did anything. The zero comes off the gradebook, and I want it in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. Put the time and the room in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay under procedure 4.4, on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still demand the zero removed from the gradebook and everything above confirmed in writing, including the time and room. I expect your answer in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted the private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook and the whole arrangement in writing with a time and room; that is the fair outcome under 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You admitted entering the zero before calling her and moved on, which gave her a first bit of ground, and then your dated, checkable evidence with answers ready for her objections earned the rewrite.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether anything was on his record unanswered through several turns, which kept her pressing on procedure instead of the evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the first edit at 11:31 PM on October 28 with the text pasted in minutes later, which sat very close to that kind of late night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you laid out the outline beside the essay, answer her revising objection before moving to the offer, so the third piece stands on its own instead of being dropped.
